title: My First Game Creation Named "Flash Run"
author: B0urBonx
selftext:
I built Flash Run, a simple browser endless runner, while I'm still learning to code. In the game, you auto-run and dodge obstacles for as long as possible. It's basic and far from perfect, but creating it taught me a lot about core game concepts like movement, collision detection, and game logic.

For anyone who wants to give it a try, here's the link: [Flash Run](https://vibecodinglist.com/projects/flash-run).

I'd love to hear your feedback, suggestions, and tips, anything that can help me improve. Go ahead, test your reflexes, and see how far you can get!

comments.author: xJohn_Snow
comments.body: Congrats on finishing your first game! Love seeing your progress with movement and collision mechanics, Flash Run is a fun start. Looking forward to seeing how you build on this!

comments.author: Downtown_Lettuce9911
comments.body: The homepage looks great very simple and user-friendly, with easy mechanics. It’s also nice that there are instructions kudos for that! The characters and objects could use a bit of improvement for a more visually pleasing look, but since this is your first game, there’s plenty of room to grow. Congrats!

comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body:
Ill say this just because its something im learning/dealing with now always start developing in a mobile view port so you can optimize for mobile and then and break points for tablet and desktop 

Stats say 60+% of all traffic online that click on links are from mobile users and only 30ish% is from desktop.

And I don't know if this next part is true or not but doing it this way is a lot easier then doing it in reverse and thats the lesson i've been taught this week lol

replies.author: B0urBonx
replies.body: Makes sense since most traffic seems to come from phones, but I'm still figuring out why it's easier this way. Definitely something I’m trying to wrap my head around!

replies.author: Trashy_io
replies.body:
Just because you'll have to change a bunch to optimize it for mobile eventually if you do it in the reverse and every time I go to change a ui or hud element its not as easy as just scaling everything down 

So thats why they say to optimize it for mobile a the start of development because in terms of releasing you will get a lot more eyes on it vs the tablet and desktop version realistically depending on the product 

you could choose to not even optimize for desktop or tablet and still capture more eyes than choosing to focus just on desktop 

Ill be honest I myself am guilty I work on my desktop but scroll through my phone for entertainment even with my pc right in-front of me

replies.author: B0urBonx
replies.body: Yeah I can relate to that since even I spend more time on mobile than desktop
